newsitem.title: USA: Ford, UAW contract sets job guarantees.
newsitem.headline: Ford, UAW contract sets job guarantees.

text.p: Ford Motor Co's tentative agreement with the United Auto Workers union means that nearly every UAW-Ford plant will remain at or above 95 percent of its eligible workforce, the union said Wednesday.
"What it says, basically, is that there is virtually no set of events that can bring the numbers below the 95 percent level," said Kark Mantyla, a spokesman for the union.

The complicated employment provision is a first for the auto industry. Here is how it works, according to a summary of the contract handed out to members of the UAW National Ford Council and reporters.
After first determining a 100 percent, or baseline, Ford-UAW employment level at the beginning of the contract, the plan puts workers into three different categories.
Those categories are: bargaining units, which are most often individual plants; groups, which consist of units in the same geographic area; and company-wide UAW employment.
When the combined total of unit workers in a group is 95 percent or less than the baseline figure, each employee who retires, quits or dies is replaced by another worker on a one-for-one basis.
The contract allows Ford to postpone the new-hire program if a unit is encountering market-driven, volume related layoffs.

When the combined number of workers in a particular group is between 95 percent and 105 percent of the base level, attrition is replaced on the same one-for-two formula that existed under the previous contract.
When the combined number of unit workers in a particular group exceeds 105 percent of the base level, attrition replacement is suspended altogether.

Ford can also suspend attrition replacement if its total number of UAW workers surpasses 110 percent of the base figure. However, that does not apply to individual groups where the level is 95 percent or less of the group's base level.
Ford has about 105,000 hourly workers in the United States represented by the UAW.
